title: shotset-provenance-journal
content:
Purpose / short goal:
- Capture an exploratory notebook for how we pick, store, and apply few-shot examples ("shotsets") for prompt-library components. Focus on metadata/provenance so we can: (a) debug failures, (b) monitor drift, (c) A/B compare selection strategies.

Context / motivation:
- We keep getting brittle model outputs when example selection is opaque. Ops wants a way to trace which example(s) caused a hallucination or classification flip. Also need to ensure shotsets are stable across model upgrades and quantization changes.

High-level desiderata for shotset provenance:
- Shot-level metadata: source_id, original_user_id (anonymized), timestamp, dataset_name, quality_label, paraphrase_group_id, canonical_form
- Selection history: why this shot was chosen (rule id or scorer id), score, rank among candidates
- Transformations: truncation, anonymization, tokenization changes, normalization steps applied
- Usage logs: model_version, embedding_version, route, latency, outcome_label (pass/fail), eval_prompt_id

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Storage size vs. auditability: do we store full original text for every shot? If not, how much context to keep (first 200 chars + checksum)?
- Privacy: PII removal at ingestion vs storing encrypted original + access controls. Requirement from compliance: retain provenance but be able to redact.
- Canonicalization: should we store a canonical form (lowercased, punctuation normalized) and keep raw? How to handle examples where canonical form loses meaning?
- Paraphrase clustering: aggressive grouping reduces diversity; conservative grouping bloats shotset sizes. Heuristic idea: cluster by cosine similarity of instruction/label embedding and require lexical overlap threshold for merge.

Selection heuristics to test (labelled heuristics for logging):
- H-RECENT: prefer most recent high-quality examples (quality>=0.8, recency score decay 30d)
- H-SIM-EMB: nearest-neighbor by embedding to the current query (top-k = 8)
- H-DIVERSE: maximize pairwise distance between selected shots (greedy farthest-first)
- H-STRAT: stratified by label distribution to match historical class priors (cap per label)
- H-BM25: lexical retrieval + fuzzy match fallback

Experiment plan (small-scale):
1) Dataset: 2k internal labeled QA pairs (mix of long-form and short-answer). Split: 70/15/15 for train/dev/test.
2) Generate candidate pool from train: apply paraphrase expansion (back-translation, T5 paraphraser) to increase candidate diversity 2.5x.
3) For each heuristic, build shotset size 1/4/8/16; run on dev queries and record metrics: accuracy, calibration (ECE), hallucination-rate (manual label), token-overhead, avg-latency.
4) Add metric: provenance-entropy = how many distinct sources contribute to final answer across test set; lower = higher dependence on fewer examples.
5) Log full selection trace for sample of failures (store selected shot ids + scores + transformations).

Quick notes from initial runs (2024-11 pilot):
- H-SIM-EMB (k=8) improved top-1 accuracy by +4.2% over random but increased hallucination rate on long-form items by +2.6% (likely due to overfit to phrasing).
- H-DIVERSE reduced hallucinations but dropped exact-match accuracy on concise answers; tradeoff between generative style and factual precision.
- Paraphrase expansion added helpful variants but introduced noisy paraphrases that changed label meaning ~1.1% of time. Need paraphrase filter.

Shot schema proposal (single-line keys):
- shot_id: string (uuid)
- source: string ("query-log", "manual-curation", "benchmark")
- dataset: string
- anonymized_source_id: string
- ts: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ
- quality_score: decimal (0-1)
- canonical_text: string
- raw_text_hash: string (sha256)
- label: string
- paraphrase_group: string or null
- selection_history: comma-separated rule_ids (most recent first)
- transformations: comma-separated tokens (e.g., redaction:name,email; truncate:256)
- notes: free short text

Logging format for selection event (single string fields for easy ingestion):
- event_id | query_id | shot_ids (ordered, pipe-separated) | query_embedding_model | selection_rule | scores_csv | timestamp | use_route | model_version | outcome_tag

Operational checklist (for MVP):
- [ ] define minimal shot schema and stable ID format
- [ ] implement secure store for raw_text (encrypted) with access audit logs
- [ ] implement canonicalizer + small rule set (lowercase, unicode normalize, remove extra whitespace, redact emails/phone)
- [ ] build selection logging hook in the querying service (persist event blob to BigQuery)
- [ ] design UI for trace: show top-5 selected shots, their sources, quality, and transformations applied
- [ ] add quick toggle in dev console to re-run query with alternative shotset heuristics for debugging

Sample candidate shots (synthesized for notes):
1) shot_id: s-001 | source: manual-curation | quality:0.95 | canonical_text: "How do I revoke an API key?" | label: "steps_to_revoke_api_key: list"
2) shot_id: s-002 | source: query-log | quality:0.82 | canonical_text: "delete access token for user" | label: "steps_to_revoke_api_key: list" (paraphrase_group: p-14)
3) shot_id: s-103 | source: benchmark | quality:0.99 | canonical_text: "What is the difference between quantization and pruning?" | label: "short_explain: paragraph"

Example of a failure trace (toy):
- query_id q-77: "how to revoke api token for service account"
- selected shots: s-002 (score 0.87), s-001 (0.72), s-103 (0.12)
- transformations: s-002(redact:emails); s-001(none)
- outcome: model returned steps referencing IAM roles instead of token revocation -> manual label: hallucination: true
- next steps: add negative example where answer "IAM roles" is wrong for token revocation; adjust retrieval to bias towards explicit token vocab.

Hypotheses to test next:
- H1: keeping raw_text_hash + minimal prefix (100 chars) + encrypted raw store reduces audit storage by ~60% while keeping ability to reproduce error at 90% fidelity.
- H2: paraphrase_group deduping (keep 1 representative per group) reduces hallucination rate by focusing on higher-quality lexical forms.
- H3: selection_rule ensembles (mix H-SIM-EMB top-4 + H-DIVERSE top-4) give better precision-recall tradeoff than single-rule systems.

Short-term TODOs (pri):
- Liam: spin up small BigQuery table schema and example ingestion pipeline (deadline 2025-01-10)
- Chen: prototype paraphrase filter that flags label-changing paraphrases (2025-01-17)
- Priya (me): wire up dev console debug toggle + design mini-UI mock (2025-01-24)

Notes to self (informal):
- keep filenames terse when storing raw shots (s-UUID.txt), but store shot metadata in a single shot registry CSV for quick lookup.
- remember to add unit tests around canonicalizer (cases: emoji, non-ascii punctuation).
- ask privacy legal about storing hashed user identifiers vs synthetic pseudonyms.

Meeting crumbs / references:
- convo w/ SRE 2024-11-06 about log retention limits (SRE asked to cap at 90 days before archiving)
- Linear ticket: ISSUE-482 (shotset provenance)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/shotset-tools#37 (paraphrase expansion prototype)

End-of-note. This is a living scratchpad — expect fragments and TODOs. Will move to shared doc once we settle schema and initial pipeline.
